title: CRASH-073: parseurl scheme colon slash just path length not decremented oob read (out-of-bounds-read)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:heap-buffer-overflow at Zend/zend_alloc.c:403 in _estrndup when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src 6fcc1515cba0d4719bf1edd831d242db9bc72f0f, which postdates the release, and names the defect at ext/standard/url.c:143 (defect) / ext/standard/url.c:292 (faulting estrndup)
fidelity: the corpus's own trigger script, run through the real interpreter (PHP's cli SAPI, ext/standard only, the port's 145 translation units) rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build completes it natively, so an arm that completes it saw nothing.

virtual-malloc.oracle: the case on the virtual profile with the seam present but returning every freed block's loan, so only musl mallocng revokes, per BLOCK, when PHP's cache hands a block back to free(): a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json php-real-block)
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: reached (the stock arm ran this case to its normal end, the corpus's pristine record says it completes, and revocation-sanity completed on this arm) and completed with no fault; completed but its output differs from the corpus's pristine record (136 lines vs 6); the stock arm's output differs from the corpus's pristine record (reported, not gated: see the module docstring on the deviation)
